recentItems.title: Do your acts of kindness make a real impact? | Jon Bogard | TEDxWUSTL
recentItems.description:
What if just doing some good isn’t actually good enough? Jon Bogard challenges us to confront the uncomfortable truth: Our instincts about helping others are often flawed. Cognitive “bugs” like opportunity cost neglect, the “warm glow” feeling of giving, and scope insensitivity lead us to make choices that selfishly feel meaningful but fall short of real impact.

Given that the world’s problems are bigger than the number of people rushing in to help, how can we use our lives to do the most good possible? What if just doing some good isn’t actually good enough? 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Neighbours need each other for a handful of ash | Mehmet Sait Uyanık | TEDxVitosha
recentItems.description: Climate disasters don’t respect borders or visas - when they strike, the only question is how fast we can help one another. With COP31 approaching, Ambassador of Türkiye to Bulgaria Mehmet Sait Uyanık reveals how navigating geopolitics and climate justice at the crossroads of three continents proves that global solidarity is our only path forward. With a strong focus on COP31, Ambassador Mehmet Sait Uyanık brings Türkiye’s climate policies to the forefront. He shares the experience of a  nation situated between Europe, Asia, and the Middle East to tackle geopolitics, energy, and climate justice, and to accelerate global electrification and Net Zero emissions. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How We Talk Shapes What We Share | Mahnaz Lashkri | TEDxEuropean University Institute Florence
recentItems.description:
Rivers do not stop at borders, so who decides how their water is shared? 
Mahnaz Lashkri turns to transnational water governance, one of the world’s most contested resources, and shows how the way we talk shapes what we share. A resource that crosses borders needs conversations that cross them too.

This talk was part of the first edition of TEDxEuropean University Institute Florence, held at Palazzo Buontalenti, home to the Florence School of Transnational Governance of the European University Institute (EUI), in the former courtroom of the Court of Appeal of Florence (Italy).

Theme: “Agents of Change”. Mahnaz Lashkri is Strategic Projects and Partnerships Manager at the University of Kurdistan Hewlêr (UKH). She is a co-founding member of UKH’s Center for Peacebuilding and Dialogue. She holds a BA with honours in Politics and International Relations and an MA in International Studies, both from UKH. 
She has worked in government and the humanitarian sector on policy, community-led advocacy, project management, and media and communications. She is an alumna of the Global Shapers Community and the US State Department. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How Online Actions Become Crises | Margarita Iliopoulou | TEDxEuropean University Institute Florence
recentItems.description:
A reaction on social media takes a second. Margarita Iliopoulou asks whether it matters far more than you think, linking it to digital bank runs and misinformation. In a financial system that runs on trust, what spreads online can have real consequences.

This talk was part of the first edition of TEDxEuropean University Institute Florence, held at Palazzo Buontalenti, home to the Florence School of Transnational Governance of the European University Institute (EUI), in the former courtroom of the Court of Appeal of Florence (Italy).

Theme: “Agents of Change”. Margarita Iliopoulou is Senior Legal Expert at the EU Single Resolution Board. She is a legal counsel and economist specialising in banking regulation and digital transformation. She has advised on banking supervision and resolution across six jurisdictions, from Berlin to Washington. Her work has taken her across EU institutions and international organisations in Italy, Belgium, Greece and the UK, with a focus on sustainable finance and digital innovation. 
She is also committed to pro bono work on transparency and anti-corruption. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: A Musical Experience with Pavan Bhat | Pavan Bhat | TEDxGCEM
recentItems.description:
The joy of music with Pavan Bhat at TEDxGCEM.

Through a captivating musical session, Pavan Bhat brought rhythm, melody, and energy to the TEDxGCEM stage, creating a memorable experience for the audience. 

This musical session celebrates the power of music to transcend words, evoke emotions, and bring people together.

Because sometimes, a melody is all it takes to create a connection.

 

 Pavan Bhat is a Kannada singer, performer, and storyteller who is on a mission to bring people together through music. Known for his Kannada Retro-Jamming experiences, Pavan has created a unique space where audiences don’t just listen to music; they sing along, participate, and become part of the performance. From children and young adults to parents and senior citizens, his shows bring generations together through the nostalgia and emotion of Kannada music. What began as a passion for music has grown into a community-driven movement, with Pavan performing across Karnataka and creating experiences that celebrate Kannada culture, connection, and togetherness. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: WHO TAUGHT YOU WHAT TO BECOME? | Kinanti Sakalaguna Prasetyo | TEDxCRIBS Youth
recentItems.description:
What if... the person you were meant to become isn't the person everyone expects you to be? Who shaped us into the people we want to be? Now I want you guys to think about it for a moment. Then, picture this. An elite boarding school. Generations of students prepared to become doctors, lawyers, even engineers — people who will eventually become somebody.
 A student at Cahaya Rancamaya with a passion for movies, books, and storytelling. She is
curious about individuality, success, and the expectations society places on young people. After
an unsuccessful attempt to join TEDx in Grade 10, she tried again the following year and earned
a place in the program. Through her TEDx talk, she hopes to challenge conventional definitions
of success and encourage others to discover their own paths to fulfillment. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why Visibility Feels Scarier Than Failure | Taylor M. LaSane | TEDxBuckheadAve
recentItems.description:
What if you're not afraid of failing, but afraid of being seen succeeding? Taylor M. LaSane explores how success can threaten our sense of belonging, causing us to hide from our own potential. She challenges us to rethink what holds us back and find the courage to be visible before we feel ready. "Taylor M. LaSane is a consultant, facilitator, and founder of SHYNE, a career studio helping leaders navigate change. A certified leadership coach trained through Brown University and Harvard Business School Online, Taylor combines executive strategy, neuroscience, and Scripture to help people move from uncertainty to intentional action.

Taylor spent nearly a decade at Google leading executive communications and organizational change initiatives impacting more than 150,000 employees globally. Today, she brings that same strategic lens to individuals, teams, and organizations navigating growth, transformation, and visibility.  A Detroit native, wife, twin mom, and Howard University alumna, Taylor guides international audiences on career clarity, leadership, visibility, and navigating change with intention. Her work is grounded in a simple idea: who you are is the foundation for what you do." This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: 起点好，不如习惯好 | Chienchou Shen | TEDxGrand School Qingdao Youth
recentItems.description:
沈建州围绕“起点好不如习惯好”，指出原生家庭0—4岁的互动方式会奠定孩子终生的人格底色，父母常无意识地复制自己童年的沟通模式。本次演讲重点分享了倾听、恳谈、回应、暗示、道歉与宽恕等“人格学分”，强调父母每天的语言和回应会变成孩子未来的信念。最后提出好习惯一旦养成便难以改变，建议通过写下来、找教练、找对人、坚持21次、用好习惯置换坏习惯来培养。核心结论是：父母给不了孩子自己没有的智慧和习惯，但可以给自己成长的勇气和决心，从倾听、欣赏、道歉、陪伴等日常行动开始改变。 Chienchou Shen is a renowned family education expert, bestselling author, and corporate consultant with over 25 years of experience in family growth and 30 years in corporate advisory. He is the founder of the "Three-Set Lifetime System" and a certified psychological counselor.
 As a highly sought-after speaker, he has delivered over 2,500 public speeches, led more than 500 youth training camps, and provided over 10,000 individual coaching cases. He is the author of six bestselling books, including "A Good Starting Point is Not as Good as Good Habits" and "It's All Parents' Fault." He has also served as the CEO of multinational companies and is a film producer.
 Currently serving as the Chief Special Guest Mentor at iJIA Family Growth Academy, his core philosophy is: Respect differences, live out your strengths, and recognize that everyone is unique. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The moon is not round | Taihong Pan | TEDxGrand School Qingdao Youth
recentItems.description: In this TED Talk, Taihong Pan shares how a small, scratched 300-yuan telescope on a sixth-floor balcony changed the way he sees the sky—and himself. The first time he looked at the moon, he screamed: it wasn't the smooth, shiny coin he'd imagined, but a rocky, pitted world. That shock sparked a habit of questioning what he thought he knew. Through his father, he learned Venus is a planet, not a star; through The Space Encyclopedia, he discovered that Chang'e is not just a fairy tale but a real lunar probe that brought 1,731 grams of moon soil home. He also speaks honestly about nearly giving up on a math problem, watching rockets explode and be rebuilt, and realizing that space exploration depends on thousands of unnamed workers, not just famous astronauts. His message: being wrong is not failure—every corrected mistake brings us closer to the real sky. Chasing stars isn't about catching one; it's about keeping your head up, keep asking questions, and keep being surprised. As a student at Grand Primary School,Taihong Pan has achieved notable recognition in several English competitions. He won the Platinum Award in the Individual Final of the 20th Qingdao "Future Star" English Competition for Primary and Secondary School Students, and earned Gold Awards in the Individual Finals of the 17th, 18th, and 19th Qingdao English Competitions for Primary and Secondary School Students. He was also awarded Gold in the Individual Finals of the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Peinuo Cup TED English Speech Competitions. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: A Letter to My Future Daughter | Mark Hsueh | TEDxGUIS Guangzhou Youth
recentItems.description: In this deeply personal and reflective talk, Mark Hsueh explores the hopes, values, and life lessons he wishes to pass on to the next generation. Through the imagined form of a letter to his future daughter, he reflects on love, family, identity, and the kind of world he hopes she will grow up in. Beyond the expectations of parenthood, Mark invites us to consider what truly matters when shaping another person's future: the values we model, the wisdom we share, and the freedom we give others to discover their own paths. His talk offers a thoughtful reflection on legacy, responsibility, and the enduring power of love. Teacher of English at Guangzhou Ulink International School-NCPA Division This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why your career needs a map, not a ladder | Meryem Ben Elajla | TEDxVUB
recentItems.description:
What if your career wasn't meant to follow a straight line? Meryem challenges the traditional idea of climbing the career ladder, encouraging us to see our professional journeys as maps filled with different paths, unexpected turns, and endless opportunities. Meryem Ben Elajla, photonics expert, deep-tech professional, and someone whose career has taken her across research, technology, business and everything in between.

Having explored so many different paths, Meryem knows firsthand that a career rarely moves in one straight direction. In her talk, she challenges the traditional career ladder and asks: what if we stopped climbing and started mapping instead? This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: L'Union Européenne, dans tous ses états ! | Sylvain Kahn | TEDxVersailles Grand Parc
recentItems.description:
Dans quel État vivez-vous ? La France, l’Estonie, le Portugal… Personne ne répond « l’Union européenne ». Depuis le fameux « objet politique non identifié » de Jacques Delors, on a pris l’habitude de ne pas trop se demander ce qu’elle est vraiment.

L’historien Sylvain Kahn propose de briser ce tabou. Selon lui, l’UE est un État, à sa manière. Les Européens ont inventé des cités-États, des monarchies, des empires, et même un Saint-Empire qui a duré mille ans ; l’Union serait simplement la dernière de ces formes. Il montre le moment où, selon lui, elle a basculé : la nuit du 20 au 21 juillet 2020, quand les Vingt-Sept ont décidé d’emprunter ensemble 750 milliards d’euros sur les marchés pour faire face au Covid. Une monnaie, une cour de justice, des lois votées par des élus : c’est un « État d’États », qui met en réseau la souveraineté de ses membres au lieu de la leur prendre.

Et si l’on reconnaissait que nous avons deux États, la question ne serait plus « faut-il en sortir ? » mais « qu’est-ce qu’on veut en faire ? ». Sylvain Kahn est professeur à Sciences Po. Agrégé d'histoire et docteur en géographie, il est chercheur au Centre d'histoire de Sciences Po, où il étudie l'Union européenne : son histoire, sa géographie politique, son régime et sa vie politique, son interaction avec le reste du monde. Ancien producteur de l'émission Planète Terre sur France Culture, il est l'auteur de plusieurs ouvrages de référence aux PUF et chez CNRS Éditions. Son dernier livre, L'Europe : un État qui s'ignore, fruit de vingt ans de recherches, démontre que l'Union européenne est déjà, en actes, un État supranational et baroque. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
